```csharp
    private static Sprite? _textButtonSprite;
    private static Sprite? _fullScreenSprite;
    private static Sprite? _closeButtonSprite;
    private static TextMeshPro? _textPrefab;
    private static bool _triedInit = false;

    public static Sprite? PopUpBackSprite => TryGet(ref _popUpBackSprite, 3);
    public static Sprite? TextButtonSprite => TryGet(ref _textButtonSprite, 2);
    public static Sprite? FullScreenSprite => TryGet(ref _fullScreenSprite, 0);
    
    public static TextMeshPro? TextPrefab
    {
        get
        {
            EnsureLoaded();
            return _textPrefab;
        }
    }

    private static Sprite? TryGet(ref Sprite? field, int childIndex)
    {
        EnsureLoaded();
        return field;
    }

    private static void EnsureLoaded()
    {
        if (_triedInit) return;
        _triedInit = true;
        try
        {
            var twitch = TwitchManager.Instance;
            if (twitch == null) return;
            var popUp = twitch.transform.GetChild(0);
            _fullScreenSprite = popUp.GetChild(0).GetComponent<SpriteRenderer>().sprite;
            _textButtonSprite = popUp.GetChild(2).GetComponent<SpriteRenderer>().sprite;
            _popUpBackSprite = popUp.GetChild(3).GetComponent<SpriteRenderer>().sprite;
            
            _textPrefab = Object.Instantiate(popUp.GetChild(1).GetComponent<TextMeshPro>(), null);
            _textPrefab.gameObject.hideFlags = HideFlags.HideAndDontSave;
            Object.DontDestroyOnLoad(_textPrefab.gameObject);
        }
        catch { /* 忽略，资源未就绪 */ }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// 获取白色Sprite（始终可用）

    public static Sprite WhiteSprite
    {
        get

            if (_whiteSprite != null) return _whiteSprite;
            var tex = Texture2D.whiteTexture;
            _whiteSprite = Sprite.Create(tex, new Rect(0, 0, tex.width, tex.height), new Vector2(0.5f, 0.5f), 100f);
            return _whiteSprite;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>

    /// </summary>
    public static Sprite GetWindowSprite() => PopUpBackSprite ?? WhiteSprite;
}
```

```csharp
        var obj = new GameObject("VerticalHolder");
        obj.layer = LayerMask.NameToLayer("UI");
        
        float totalHeight = 0;
        float maxWidth = 0;
        var children = new List<(GameObject go, GUISize size)>();
        
        foreach (var widget in _widgets)
        {
            if (widget == null) continue;
            var childObj = widget.Instantiate(available, out var childSize);
            if (childObj != null)
            {
                childObj.transform.SetParent(obj.transform, false);
                children.Add((childObj, childSize));
                totalHeight += childSize.Height;
                maxWidth = Mathf.Max(maxWidth, childSize.Width);
            }
            else
            {
                // Even null objects contribute to height (e.g., margins)
                totalHeight += childSize.Height;
                maxWidth = Mathf.Max(maxWidth, childSize.Width);
            }
        }
        
        // Position children from top to bottom
        float y = totalHeight / 2;
        foreach (var (childObj, childSize) in children)
        {
            y -= childSize.Height / 2;
            childObj.transform.localPosition = new Vector3(0, y, 0);
            y -= childSize.Height / 2;
        }
        
        actualSize = new GUISize(maxWidth, totalHeight);
        return obj;
    }
}
```

toolCalls.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).

toolCalls.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

toolCalls.description:
Replaces text within a file. Use this tool for targeted edits to existing files.

The tool replaces exactly ONE occurrence of `old_string` with `new_string` by default. The `old_string` MUST uniquely identify the specific instance to change — unless `replace_all` is set to true, in which case every occurrence of `old_string` will be replaced. Use the read_file tool to establish the current file state before the first text replacement. If the tool reports that the file changed since it was read, re-read it before retrying.

If you need to replace the full contents of an existing file, use `write_file` instead.
If `old_string` is empty, the tool treats the operation as creating a new file. This is only valid when the target file does not already exist.
Do not use an empty `old_string` to overwrite an existing file.

The user has the ability to modify the `new_string` content. If modified, this will be stated in the response.

Expectation for required parameters:
1. `file_path` MUST be an absolute path; otherwise an error will be thrown.
2. Prefer exact literal text for `old_string`, including relevant surrounding context and matching whitespace, indentation, and newlines when possible.
3. Prefer exact literal text for `new_string`, and ensure the resulting code is correct and idiomatic.
4. NEVER escape `old_string` or `new_string`, that would break the exact literal text requirement.

**Important:** Exact literal matches are the most reliable. The tool may also apply limited deterministic normalization for whitespace, indentation, and escaping, but do not rely on fallback matching when you can provide the exact text. The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

toolCalls.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

args.content:
# UI 系统重写计划 — 使用 Unity UI (Canvas/RectTransform)

## 目标
将现有 `UI/Window/` 下的 GUI 系统从 SpriteRenderer 改为 Unity UI 系统（Canvas、RectTransform、UnityEngine.UI.Image、TextMeshProUGUI），保持与 Nebula 90% 相似的 API 结构。用户会自定义所有材质。

## 核心改动
- SpriteRenderer → UnityEngine.UI.Image (with RectTransform)
- BoxCollider2D → 无需碰撞体（Unity UI 使用 Raycaster + Canvas）
- PassiveButton 仍可用（Among Us 的 PassiveButton 兼容 UI 层）
- 所有 Widget 使用 RectTransform 布局
- MetaScreen 改为使用 Canvas + RectTransform

## 文件结构 (全部在 UI/Window/)

### 1. GUI.cs — 核心抽象（重写）
- `GUIAlignment` — 保留
- `GUISize` — 改用 Vector2 兼容
- `TextStyle` — 保留，增加 TMP_FontAsset 字段
- `GUIWidget` — 抽象类，Instantiate 改为返回 RectTransform
- `IGUIScreen` — SetWidget 签名改为接受 GUIWidget
- `GUIClickable` — 保留
- `GUIClickAction` — 保留
- `IGUI` — 工厂接口，签名与 Nebula GUI 接口 90% 相似

### 2. VanillaAsset.cs — 资源缓存（重写）
- 延迟加载 Among Us 原生 Sprite
- 新增 `CreateText(RectTransform parent)` 返回 TextMeshProUGUI
- 新增 `CreateImage(RectTransform parent)` 返回 UnityEngine.UI.Image
- 保留 WhiteSprite 降级

### 3. Widgets.cs — 具体控件（重写）
- `EmptyWidget` — 返回 null
- `TextWidget` — 用 TextMeshProUGUI
- `ButtonWidget` — 用 Image + TextMeshProUGUI + PassiveButton
- `ImageWidget` — 用 UnityEngine.UI.Image
- `VerticalHolderWidget` — 用 VerticalLayoutGroup 或手动 RectTransform
- `HorizontalHolderWidget` — 用 HorizontalLayoutGroup 或手动
- `MarginWidget` — LayoutElement 或空占位

### 4. MetaScreen.cs — 屏幕（重写）
- 改为 MonoBehaviour + Canvas
- `GenerateWindow` 创建 Canvas、Background Image、Close Button
- `SetWidget` 清空并实例化 Widget
- `Close` 销毁整个 GameObject
- 保留 `CreateWindow(string)` 兼容现有调用

### 5. LIDGUI.cs — 工厂实现（小幅调整）
- 方法签名匹配新 IGUI

### 6. MetaUI.cs — 高级辅助（保留+接入）
- OpenButtonWindow, OpenConfirmDialog, OpenMessageDialog, OpenTextWindow, OpenCustomWindow
- 接入新的系统

### 7. GUIWidgetHelpers.cs — 新增（参考 Nebula）
- WithRoom, Move, Enmask 等扩展方法

## 验证
- `dotnet build` 编译通过
- 0 错误

Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the job and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool
Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:
- Complex multi-step tasks - When a job requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Work that requires careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a job list to track the work
- User explicitly requests job list - When the user directly asks you to use the job list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as jobs
- When you start working on a job - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a job - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up jobs discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool
Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward job
- The job is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The job can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The job is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial job to do. In this case you are better off just doing the job directly.

## Job Fields
- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: Detailed description of what needs to be done, including context and acceptance criteria
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when job is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). This is displayed to the user while you work on the job.

**IMPORTANT**: Always provide activeForm when creating jobs. The subject should be imperative ("Run tests") while activeForm should be present continuous ("Running tests"). All jobs are created with status `pending`.

- Create jobs with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- Include enough detail in the description for another agent to understand and complete the job
- After creating jobs, use job_update to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check job_list first to avoid creating duplicate jobs
- Use `allowDuplicate: true` only when you intentionally need a second open job with the same normalized subject

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```

Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

This tool executes a given shell command using the best available Windows shell (PowerShell Core, Windows PowerShell, or Command Prompt).

IMPORTANT:
- This tool is for terminal operations (e.g., git / npm / docker / build & test commands).
- DO NOT use this tool for file operations like reading, writing, editing, or searching files. Prefer the dedicated file tools for those actions.
- Quote any file path that contains spaces with double quotes, e.g. `cd "/path with spaces"` or `python "/path with spaces/script.py"`.
- If a command would produce very large output, prefer adding flags/filters (narrow paths, limit counts, request specific fields, machine-readable formats like JSON) to keep output small and unambiguous.
- Very large outputs may be returned as the most recent tail of the output. Earlier content may be truncated from the beginning. If the tool reports a "Full output saved to: <path>", that file contains the full command output. Use the exact path returned by the tool, then prefer searching that file first (grep/rg or platform equivalents) for specific ERROR/WARN/FAIL/SUCCESS markers, then reading small slices (with `read_file` using `offset`/`limit`) or tailing the log file instead of re-running expensive commands.
- Do not append truncating pipelines such as `| tail`, `| Select-Object -Last`, or similar to an expensive first run just to suppress output. Those discard earlier context and force a re-run if you later need omitted lines. Let the tool/log capture the full output, then inspect the saved log file.
- When issuing multiple shell commands in one response, parallelize only when they are truly independent and do not compete for the same files, directories, logs, locks, caches, git state, or ports. If one command depends on another or shared state may race, run them sequentially.

The following information is returned:
- Command: Executed command.
- Directory: Directory where command was executed, or `(root)`.
- Output: Combined command output (stdout/stderr). Can be `(empty)` or an excerpt if very large.
- Error: Error or `(none)` if no error was reported for the subprocess.
- Exit Code: Exit code or `(none)` if terminated by signal.
- Signal: Signal number or `(none)` if no signal was received.

The tool replaces exactly ONE occurrence of `old_string` with `new_string` by default. In C#, default interface methods are only available on the interface, not on the implementing class when called through the class type. The fix is to either:
1. Make LIDGUI explicitly implement these methods, or
2. Use `IGUI` interface type instead of `LIDGUI` concrete type when calling

The simplest fix is to change the callers to use `IGUI` instead of `LIDGUI`, or add the missing methods to `LIDGUI`. Let me add the missing methods to `LIDGUI` since the callers use `LIDGUI.Instance`.</think>问题是 `RawButton`、`VerticalMargin` 和 `HorizontalMargin` 在接口上是默认方法，但 `LIDGUI` 类没有继承它们。我需要将它们添加到 `LIDGUI` 中。

toolCalls.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

编译成功，0 错误，仅剩 3 个既有警告（非本次改动引入）。

### 改动总结

整个 `UI/Window/` 已从 SpriteRenderer 体系重写为 **Unity UI 体系**（Canvas / RectTransform / `UnityEngine.UI.Image` / `TextMeshProUGUI`），与 Nebula API 保持 ~90% 相似的接口设计。

### 文件清单（`UI/Window/`）

| 文件 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| **GUI.cs** | 核心抽象：`GUIAlignment`、`GUISize`、`FuzzySize`、`TextStyle`、`GUIWidget`、`IGUIScreen`、`GUIClickable`、`IGUI` 工厂接口（含 default method 简化调用） |
| **VanillaAsset.cs** | 原生资源缓存 + `CreateImage()` / `CreateText()` / `ApplyAlignment()` 辅助方法（用户可自定义材质） |
| **Widgets.cs** | `EmptyWidget`、`TextWidget`、`RealtimeTextWidget`、`ButtonWidget`、`ImageWidget`、`VerticalHolderWidget`、`HorizontalHolderWidget`、`ArrangeWidget`、`MarginWidget` |
| **MetaScreen.cs** | `MonoBehaviour` + Canvas 窗口：`GenerateWindow`、`GenerateBlankWindow`、`SetWidget`、`Close`、`CreateWindow` |
| **LIDGUI.cs** | `IGUI` 工厂实现 + `GUI.API` 静态入口 |
| **MetaUI.cs** | 高级辅助：`OpenButtonWindow`、`OpenConfirmDialog`、`OpenMessageDialog`、`OpenTextWindow`、`OpenCustomWindow` |
| **GUIWidgetHelpers.cs** | 扩展方法：`WithRoom`、`Move` |

### 与 Nebula 的对应关系

| Nebula | LightInDark |
|---|---|
| `Virial.Media.GUI` 接口 | `IGUI` 接口 |
| `NebulaAPI.GUI` | `GUI.API` / `LIDGUI.Instance` |
| `GUIWidget.Instantiate(Size, out Size)` | `GUIWidget.Instantiate(GUISize, out GUISize)` |
| `GUIScreen.SetWidget` | `IGUIScreen.SetWidget` |
| `MetaScreen` (MonoBehaviour) | `MetaScreen` (MonoBehaviour) |
| `MetaDialog.OpenDialog` | `MetaUI.OpenMessageDialog` / `OpenConfirmDialog` |
| `GUIWidgetHelpers` | `GUIWidgetHelpers` |

### 关键变化

- `SpriteRenderer` → `UnityEngine.UI.Image`（Sliced 类型）
- `BoxCollider2D` → 移除（Unity UI 用 `raycastTarget` 替代）
- `TextMeshPro` → `TextMeshProUGUI`
- 所有 Widget 返回带 `RectTransform` 的 GameObject
- `PassiveButton` 保留（Among Us 原生组件，兼容 UI 层）

Now I have a complete picture. Let me compile the thorough findings.

---

## Comprehensive Nebula GUI System Analysis

### 1. ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW

The Nebula GUI system consists of three layers:
- **API Layer** (`NebulaAPI/Media/GUI.cs` + `NebulaAPI/Text/Text.cs`) — defines interfaces and abstract classes
- **Implementation Layer** (`NebulaPluginNova/Modules/MetaWidget/GUIWidget.cs`) — contains `NebulaGUIWidgetEngine` (the concrete `GUI` implementation)
- **Widget Classes** (`NebulaPluginNova/Modules/MetaWidget/`) — concrete widget implementations (`NoSGUIText`, `NoSGUIImage`, `GUIButton`, `GUIModernButton`, etc.)

---

### 2. KEY CORE CLASSES

#### `GUIWidget` (abstract base class, in `GUI.cs` of `NebulaAPI/Media`)
```csharp
public abstract class GUIWidget
{
    internal abstract GUIAlignment Alignment { get; }
    internal virtual Image? BackImage { get; set; }
    internal virtual bool GrayoutedBackImage { get; set; }
    internal abstract GameObject? Instantiate(Size size, out Size actualSize);
    internal abstract GameObject? Instantiate(Anchor anchor, Size size, out Size actualSize);
    public virtual bool PostponesConsideringSize { get; set; } = false;
    public static implicit operator GUIWidgetSupplier(GUIWidget? widget) => () => widget ?? NebulaAPI.GUI.EmptyWidget;
}
```

#### `AbstractGUIWidget` (intermediate base, in `GUIWidget.cs` of `MetaWidget`)
- Implements `Instantiate(Anchor, Size, out Size)` — calls `Instantiate(size, out actualSize)`, then positions the GameObject using `anchor.anchoredPosition` with pivot offset calculation:
  ```csharp
  localPos = anchor.anchoredPosition.ToUnityVector() - 
      new Vector3(actualSize.Width * (anchor.pivot.x - 0.5f), 
                   actualSize.Height * (anchor.pivot.y - 0.5f), 0f);
  ```
- Contains helper static methods `CalcWidth()` and `CalcHeight()` using `GUIAlignment` flags

#### `GUI` interface (in `NebulaAPI/Media/GUI.cs`)
Defines the factory methods:
- `EmptyWidget`, `RawText()`, `LocalizedText()`, `Text()`, `RealtimeText()`
- `Button()`, `ModernButton()`, `SpinButton()`
- `Image()`, `RoleIcon()`
- `ScrollView()`, `VerticalHolder()`, `HorizontalHolder()`, `Arrange()`
- `Margin()`, `GetFont()`, `GetAttribute()`, `GenerateAttribute()`
- `Masked()`, `ButtonGrouped()`, `Logic()`, `FixSize()`
- Various `TextComponent` factory methods

#### `NebulaGUIWidgetEngine` (concrete implementation of `GUI`)
- Singleton: `NebulaGUIWidgetEngine.Instance` (accessed via `GUI.API` or `NebulaAPI.GUI`)
- Contains dictionaries `allAttr` and `allAttrAsset` for caching `TextAttribute` objects
- Defines the mapping from `AttributeAsset` enum to `TextAttribute` configurations
- Each factory method returns a specific widget instance

---

### 3. WIDGET CLASSES — HOW THEY CREATE GAMEOBJECTS

#### **NoSGUIText** (`GUIText.cs`)
- **GameObject creation**: `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(VanillaAsset.StandardTextPrefab, null)` — **clones the vanilla TextMeshPro prefab**
- **Components used**: `TextMeshPro` (from prefab), optionally `BoxCollider2D` + `PassiveButton` (via `SetUpButton`)
- **TextMeshPro configuration** via `ReflectMyAttribute()` / `ReflectAttribute()`:
  - Sets `text.color`, `text.alignment`, `text.fontStyle`, `text.fontSize`, `text.fontSizeMin`, `text.fontSizeMax`, `text.enableAutoSizing`, `text.enableWordWrapping`
  - Sets `text.rectTransform.sizeDelta = new(Mathn.Min(width, attr.Size.Width), attr.Size.Height)`
  - Sets `text.rectTransform.anchorMin/Max/Pivot` to `(0.5, 0.5)` — **centered pivot**
  - Sets `text.font`, `text.fontMaterial` from `attr.Font`
  - Sets outline thickness via `text.SetOutlineThickness(attr.OutlineWidth.Value)`
  - Calls `text.UseRoleIcon()`
  - Sets `text.sortingOrder = 10`
- **Size measurement**: After `ForceMeshUpdate()`, if `IsFlexible`:
  - If `enableWordWrapping`: `text.rectTransform.sizeDelta = new(width, text.textBounds.size.y)`
  - Else: `text.rectTransform.sizeDelta = new(preferredWidth, preferredHeight)`
  - Returns `actualSize = new Size(text.rectTransform.sizeDelta)`
- **Collider/button**: Only added if `AllowGenerateCollider` is true (default true, but `GUIButton` overrides to false)

#### **NoSGUIImage** (`GUIImage.cs`)
- **GameObject creation**: `UnityHelper.CreateObject<SpriteRenderer>("Image", null, Vector3.zero, LayerExpansion.GetUILayer())` — **creates a new GameObject with SpriteRenderer**
- **Components used**: `SpriteRenderer`, optionally `BoxCollider2D` + `PassiveButton`
- **SpriteRenderer setup**:
  - `renderer.sprite = Image.GetSprite()`
  - `renderer.sortingOrder = 10`
  - If `IsMasked`: `renderer.maskInteraction = SpriteMaskInteraction.VisibleInsideMask`
- **Size calculation**: Gets `spriteSize = renderer.sprite.bounds.size`, then:
  ```csharp
  float scale = Math.Min(
      Size.Width.HasValue ? (Size.Width.Value / spriteSize.x) : float.MaxValue,
      Size.Height.HasValue ? (Size.Height.Value / spriteSize.y) : float.MaxValue
  );
  renderer.transform.localScale = Vector3.one * scale;
  actualSize = new(spriteSize.x * scale, spriteSize.y * scale);
  ```
- **Button**: If `OnClick` or `Overlay` non-null, calls `renderer.gameObject.SetUpButton(false, renderer, ...)`, adds `BoxCollider2D` with `collider.size = renderer.sprite.bounds.size`, `collider.isTrigger = true`
- **Click handling**: `button.OnClick.AddListener(() => { VanillaAsset.PlaySelectSE(); OnClick.Invoke(clickable); })`

#### **GUIButton** (`GUIButton.cs`)
- **Extends**: `NoSGUIText`
- **Overrides**: `AllowGenerateCollider => false`
- **GameObject creation**: 
  1. First calls `base.Instantiate(size, out actualSize)` to get the text GameObject
  2. Creates a **new** `SpriteRenderer` via `UnityHelper.CreateObject<SpriteRenderer>("Button", null, ...)`
  3. Sets `button.sprite = IsModern ? modernButtonSprite.GetSprite(0) : VanillaAsset.TextButtonSprite`
  4. Sets `button.drawMode = SpriteDrawMode.Sliced`, `button.tileMode = SpriteTileMode.Continuous`
  5. Sets `button.size = actualSize.ToUnityVector() + new Vector2(margin * 0.84f, margin * 0.84f)`
  6. If `AsMaskedButton`: `button.maskInteraction = SpriteMaskInteraction.VisibleInsideMask`
  7. Parents the text inner to the button: `inner.transform.SetParent(button.transform)`, offsets z by `-0.05f`
  8. Adds `BoxCollider2D` with `collider.size = actualSize + new Vector2(margin * 0.6f, margin * 0.6f)`, `collider.isTrigger = true`
  9. Calls `button.gameObject.SetUpButton(true, IsModern ? null : button, Color, SelectedColor)` to get a `PassiveButton`
  10. Returns the **button's GameObject** (parent of the text)
- **Modern mode**: Uses `modernButtonSprite` (loaded from "Nebula.Resources.GUI.Button.png"), changes sprite on hover, clears text outline, uses piled colors
- **Size adjustment**: `actualSize.Width += margin + 0.1f; actualSize.Height += margin + 0.1f;`

#### **GUIModernButton** (`GUIModernButton.cs`)
- **Extends**: `NoSGUIText` (same as `GUIButton`)
- **Overrides**: `AllowGenerateCollider => false`
- **Similar to GUIButton** but uses `modernButtonSprite` by default, supports:
  - `WithCheckMark` — adds checkmark sprite (loaded from "Nebula.Resources.GUI.Checkmark.png")
  - `SelectedDefault` / `EmphasizeOnSelected`
  - Button grouping via `GUIButtonGroupInstance`
  - `SortingGroup` component when checkmark is used
- **Sprite mapping**: `modernButtonSprite.GetSprite()` index mapping:
  - 0 = normal, 1 = hovered, 3 = selected, 4 = selected + hovered
- **Text color changes**: On hover uses `piledModernColor`, on select uses `selectedModernColor`

#### **GUISpinButton** (`GUIButton.cs`)
- **Extends**: `AbstractGUIWidget`
- Creates a **holder** GameObject with two child buttons (up/down)
- Each button: `SpriteRenderer` with `VanillaAsset.TextButtonSprite`, `BoxCollider2D`, `PassiveButton`
- Uses static `NoSGUIText` instances for "▲" and "▼" text

#### **NoSGUIFramed** (`GUIFramed.cs`)

### 11. IMPORTANT DETAILS

- **No Unity `Image` component** is used anywhere — only `SpriteRenderer` (for buttons, backgrounds, images) and `TextMeshPro` (for text)
- **`SpriteDrawMode.Sliced`** is used for button sprites and background sprites (to allow them to stretch)
- **`SpriteMaskInteraction.VisibleInsideMask`** is used for masked widgets
- **`PassiveButton`** (which is `PassiveUiElement` in Among Us) is used for all clickable elements
- **`BoxCollider2D`** with `isTrigger = true` is used for all button hitboxes
- **GameObjects are created** either via `UnityHelper.CreateObject<T>()` (which creates a new GameObject with component) or `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(prefab)` (for cloning prefabs like `StandardTextPrefab`)
- **`SortingGroup`** is used for masked views and widgets with checkmarks
- **The `Anchor` system** uses a pivot (0-1 range) and anchored position, calculated as: `localPos = anchor.anchoredPosition - actualSize * (pivot - 0.5)`

### 3. WIDGET CLASSES — HOW THEY CREATE GAMEOBJECTS

#### **NoSGUIText** (`GUIText.cs`)
- **GameObject creation**: `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(VanillaAsset.StandardTextPrefab, null)` — **clones the vanilla TextMeshPro prefab**
- **Components used**: `TextMeshPro` (from prefab), optionally `BoxCollider2D` + `PassiveButton` (via `SetUpButton`)
- **TextMeshPro configuration** via `ReflectMyAttribute()` / `ReflectAttribute()`:
  - Sets `text.color`, `text.alignment`, `text.fontStyle`, `text.fontSize`, `text.fontSizeMin`, `text.fontSizeMax`, `text.enableAutoSizing`, `text.enableWordWrapping`
  - Sets `text.rectTransform.sizeDelta = new(Mathn.Min(width, attr.Size.Width), attr.Size.Height)`
  - Sets `text.rectTransform.anchorMin/Max/Pivot` to `(0.5, 0.5)` — **centered pivot**
  - Sets `text.font`, `text.fontMaterial` from `attr.Font`
  - Sets outline thickness via `text.SetOutlineThickness(attr.OutlineWidth.Value)`
  - Calls `text.UseRoleIcon()`
  - Sets `text.sortingOrder = 10`
- **Size measurement**: After `ForceMeshUpdate()`, if `IsFlexible`:
  - If `enableWordWrapping`: `text.rectTransform.sizeDelta = new(width, text.textBounds.size.y)`
  - Else: `text.rectTransform.sizeDelta = new(preferredWidth, preferredHeight)`
  - Returns `actualSize = new Size(text.rectTransform.sizeDelta)`
- **Collider/button**: Only added if `AllowGenerateCollider` is true (default true, but `GUIButton` overrides to false)

#### **NoSGUIImage** (`GUIImage.cs`)
- **GameObject creation**: `UnityHelper.CreateObject<SpriteRenderer>("Image", null, Vector3.zero, LayerExpansion.GetUILayer())` — **creates a new GameObject with SpriteRenderer**
- **Components used**: `SpriteRenderer`, optionally `BoxCollider2D` + `PassiveButton`
- **SpriteRenderer setup**:
  - `renderer.sprite = Image.GetSprite()`
  - `renderer.sortingOrder = 10`
  - If `IsMasked`: `renderer.maskInteraction = SpriteMaskInteraction.VisibleInsideMask`
- **Size calculation**: Gets `spriteSize = renderer.sprite.bounds.size`, then:
  ```csharp
  float scale = Math.Min(
      Size.Width.HasValue ? (Size.Width.Value / spriteSize.x) : float.MaxValue,
      Size.Height.HasValue ? (Size.Height.Value / spriteSize.y) : float.MaxValue
  );
  renderer.transform.localScale = Vector3.one * scale;
  actualSize = new(spriteSize.x * scale, spriteSize.y * scale);
  ```
- **Button**: If `OnClick` or `Overlay` non-null, calls `renderer.gameObject.SetUpButton(false, renderer, ...)`, adds `BoxCollider2D` with `collider.size = renderer.sprite.bounds.size`, `collider.isTrigger = true`
- **Click handling**: `button.OnClick.AddListener(() => { VanillaAsset.PlaySelectSE(); OnClick.Invoke(clickable); })`

#### **GUIButton** (`GUIButton.cs`)
- **Extends**: `NoSGUIText`
- **Overrides**: `AllowGenerateCollider => false`
- **GameObject creation**: 
  1. First calls `base.Instantiate(size, out actualSize)` to get the text GameObject
  2. Creates a **new** `SpriteRenderer` via `UnityHelper.CreateObject<SpriteRenderer>("Button", null, ...)`

- `FontAsset.OblongMasked` → `StaticFont(VanillaAsset.OblongMaskedFontMaterial, VanillaAsset.BrookFont, true)` — Brook with mask material

#### `TextComponent` interface
```csharp
public interface TextComponent
{
    string GetString();
    string TextForCompare => GetString();
}
```
Implementations: `RawTextComponent`, `TranslateTextComponent`, `ColorTextComponent`, `LazyTextComponent`, `CombinedTextComponent`, `SizedTextComponent`

---

### 6. SIZE SYSTEM

#### `Size` struct
```csharp
public struct Size
{
    public float Width;
    public float Height;
    public Size(float width, float height);
    internal Size(UnityEngine.Vector2 size);
    internal Size(Virial.Compat.Vector2 size);
    internal UnityEngine.Vector2 ToUnityVector();
}
```

#### `FuzzySize` struct
```csharp
public struct FuzzySize
{
    public float? Width;
    public float? Height;
    public FuzzySize(float? width, float? height);
}
```
Used for images where either dimension can be null (auto-scaled to maintain aspect ratio).

---

### 7. IMAGE SYSTEM

#### `Image` interface (in `NebulaAPI/Media/Image.cs`)
```csharp
public interface Image : IManageableAsset
{
    internal UnityEngine.Sprite GetSprite();
}
```

#### `MultiImage` interface
```csharp
public interface MultiImage : IManageableAsset
{
    internal UnityEngine.Sprite GetSprite(int index);
    Image AsLoader(int index);
}
```

#### Sprite loaders used in widgets:
- `DividedExpandableSpriteLoader.FromResource("Nebula.Resources.GUI.Button.png", 150f, 12, 12, 3, 2)` — used for modern button sprites
- `DividedSpriteLoader.FromResource("Nebula.Resources.GUI.Checkmark.png", 150f, 2, 1)` — used for checkmark sprites
- `SpriteLoader.FromResource("Nebula.Resources.White.png", 100f)` — `NebulaAsset.WhiteImage`
- `ResourceExpandableSpriteLoader` — `NebulaAsset.SharpWindowBackgroundSprite`
- `SpriteLoader.FromResource("Nebula.Resources.ConfigurationGroup.png", 100f)` — configuration group background

---

### 8. BUTTON SETUP (via `SetUpButton` extension)
The extension method `gameObject.SetUpButton(...)` is called on the button's GameObject. It returns a `PassiveButton` (which is `PassiveUiElement` in Among Us). The signature varies:
- `SetUpButton(bool hasOnClickHandler, SpriteRenderer? renderer = null, Color? color = null, Color? selectedColor = null)` — adds a `PassiveButton` component, configures `OnClick`, `OnMouseOver`, `OnMouseOut` events, and sets up the renderer's color transitions

---

### 9. SPRITE/MATERIAL REFERENCES

**VanillaAsset** (loaded from `TwitchManager` popup UI):
- `StandardTextPrefab` — cloned from Twitch popup's `TextMeshPro`
- `TextButtonSprite` — from Twitch popup child 2
- `FullScreenSprite` — from Twitch popup child 0
- `PopUpBackSprite` — from Twitch popup child 3
- `CloseButtonSprite` — from `"closeButton"` asset
- `StandardMaskedFontMaterial` — `"LiberationSans SDF - BlackOutlineMasked"`
- `OblongMaskedFontMaterial` — `"Brook Atlas Material Masked"`
- `VersionFont` — `"Barlow-Medium SDF"`
- `PreSpawnFont` — `"DIN_Pro_Bold_700 SDF"`
- `BrookFont` — `"Brook SDF"`

**NebulaAsset** (loaded from asset bundle):
- `WhiteImage` — `"Nebula.Resources.White.png"` at 100 ppu
- `SharpWindowBackgroundSprite` — `"Nebula.Resources.StatisticsBackground.png"` at 100 ppu, 5x5 expandable
- Various shaders: `MultiplyShader`, `MultiplyBackShader`, `WhiteShader`, `ProgressShader`, `RoleIconShader`, etc.

---

### 10. CONCRETE FACTORY — `NebulaGUIWidgetEngine` (the `GUI.API`)

All factory methods:
| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `EmptyWidget` | `GUIEmptyWidget.Default` |
| `Image(...)` | `new NoSGUIImage(...)` with `IsMasked = true` |
| `RoleIcon(...)` | `new NoSGUIImage(...)` with `PostBuilder` setting material |
| `Button(...)` | `new GUIButton(...)` |
| `ModernButton(...)` | `new GUIModernButton(...)` |
| `SpinButton(...)` | `new GUISpinButton(...)` |
| `LocalizedText(...)` | `new NoSGUIText(...)` with `TranslateTextComponent` |
| `RawText(...)` | `new NoSGUIText(...)` with `RawTextComponent` |
| `Text(...)` | `new NoSGUIText(...)` |
| `RealtimeText(...)` | `new NoSGUIText(...)` with `PostBuilder` that updates text each frame |
| `ScrollView(...)` | `new GUIScrollView(...)` |
| `VerticalHolder(...)` | `new VerticalWidgetsHolder(...)` |
| `HorizontalHolder(...)` | `new HorizontalWidgetsHolder(...)` |
| `Arrange(...)` | Combines vertical and horizontal holders |
| `Margin(...)` | `new NoSGUIMargin(...)` |
| `Masked(...)` | `new GUIMasking(...)` |
| `ButtonGrouped(...)` | `new GUIButtonGroup(...)` |
| `Logic(...)` | `new LogicGUIWidget(...)` |
| `FixSize(...)` | `new GUISizeFixer(...)` |

---

### 11. IMPORTANT DETAILS

- **No Unity `Image` component** is used anywhere — only `SpriteRenderer` (for buttons, backgrounds, images) and `TextMeshPro` (for text)
- **`SpriteDrawMode.Sliced`** is used for button sprites and background sprites (to allow them to stretch)
- **`SpriteMaskInteraction.VisibleInsideMask`** is used for masked widgets
- **`PassiveButton`** (which is `PassiveUiElement` in Among Us) is used for all clickable elements
- **`BoxCollider2D`** with `isTrigger = true` is used for all button hitboxes
- **GameObjects are created** either via `UnityHelper.CreateObject<T>()` (which creates a new GameObject with component) or `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(prefab)` (for cloning prefabs like `StandardTextPrefab`)
- **`SortingGroup`** is used for masked views and widgets with checkmarks
- **The `Anchor` system** uses a pivot (0-1 range) and anchored position, calculated as: `localPos = anchor.anchoredPosition - actualSize * (pivot - 0.5)`

The Task tool launches specialized agents that autonomously handle complex tasks. Each agent has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

- Provide clear, detailed prompts so the agent can work autonomously and return exactly the information you need.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first. Use your judgement.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Task tool use content blocks.

assistant: First let me explore the existing auth implementation.

messages.content:
<think>Now I have a complete understanding of the Nebula GUI system. The key insight is that Nebula uses:

1. **SpriteRenderer** (not UnityEngine.UI.Image) for all visual elements - buttons, backgrounds, images
2. **TextMeshPro** (not TextMeshProUGUI) for text - cloned from `VanillaAsset.StandardTextPrefab`
3. **BoxCollider2D** with `isTrigger = true` for hit detection
4. **PassiveButton** (Among Us's `PassiveUiElement`) for click/hover handling
5. **SpriteDrawMode.Sliced** + **SpriteTileMode.Continuous** for tiling backgrounds
6. **SpriteMaskInteraction.VisibleInsideMask** for masked content
7. **UnityHelper.CreateObject<T>()** to create GameObjects with components
8. **LayerExpansion.GetUILayer()** for UI layer
9. **Anchor** system for positioning with pivot
10. **TextAttribute** system with `AttributeParams` and `AttributeAsset` enums
11. **PostponesConsideringSize** for deferred size calculation

The user said "使用Unity的UI系统" but then also said "我想做成实现也和nebula差不多，按钮等也是材质" - meaning they want it implemented similarly to Nebula, with buttons using sprites/materials.

Looking at the Nebula implementation more carefully:
- Nebula uses SpriteRenderer, NOT Unity Canvas/UI Image
- The user previously said "使用Unity的UI系统" but now wants it to be like Nebula
- Nebula's approach IS using Unity's rendering system (SpriteRenderer is a Unity component), just not the Canvas-based UGUI system

Since the user explicitly says "我想做成实现也和nebula差不多" and "按钮等也是材质", I should rewrite the system to match Nebula's approach: SpriteRenderer + TextMeshPro + BoxCollider2D + PassiveButton, with proper TextAttribute system, Anchor system, and all the widget types.

This is a major rewrite. Let me plan the files:

1. **GUI.cs** - Core types: GUIAlignment, Size, FuzzySize, Anchor, GUIWidget, GUIScreen, GUIClickable, GUIClickAction, IGUI interface (match Nebula's Virial.Media.GUI)
2. **Text.cs** - TextAttribute, FontSize, Font, TextComponent types
3. **VanillaAsset.cs** - Sprite/prefab loading (match Nebula's VanillaAsset)
4. **UnityHelper.cs** - CreateObject<T> helper, LayerExpansion
5. **Widgets.cs** - All concrete widgets: NoSGUIText, GUIButton, NoSGUIImage, NoSGUIMargin, GUIEmptyWidget, VerticalWidgetsHolder, HorizontalWidgetsHolder, GUISizeFixer, LogicGUIWidget
6. **MetaScreen.cs** - GUIScreen implementation (MetaScreen MonoBehaviour), MetaUI helpers
7. **LIDGUI.cs** - The GUI factory implementation (like NebulaGUIWidgetEngine)

This is going to be a big rewrite. Let me do it properly.

Actually, looking at the current code again and the user's request - the user previously asked to use Unity UI (Canvas/RectTransform) but now wants it to be like Nebula. Nebula uses SpriteRenderer, NOT Canvas. So I need to rewrite back to SpriteRenderer-based approach but with much more fidelity to Nebula's actual implementation.

Let me create the jobs and start implementing. This is a large task, so I'll need to be systematic.

Key things to match from Nebula:
1. `GUIWidget` with `Instantiate(Size, out Size)` and `Instantiate(Anchor, Size, out Size)`
2. `AbstractGUIWidget` with `CalcWidth`/`CalcHeight` positioning math
3. `Anchor` record with pivot + anchoredPosition
4. `Size` and `FuzzySize` structs
5. `TextAttribute` with `FontSize`, `Font`, `Color`, alignment, etc.
6. `TextComponent` interface with `RawTextComponent`, `TranslateTextComponent`, etc.
7. `NoSGUIText` cloning `VanillaAsset.StandardTextPrefab`
8. `GUIButton` extending `NoSGUIText`, adding SpriteRenderer background
9. `NoSGUIImage` with SpriteRenderer + scale-to-fit
10. `VerticalWidgetsHolder` / `HorizontalWidgetsHolder` with `PostponesConsideringSize`
11. `MetaScreen` as MonoBehaviour implementing GUIScreen
12. `SetUpButton` extension method for PassiveButton setup
13. `AttributeAsset` / `AttributeParams` enums for text styling

Let me start building this. I'll need to be pragmatic about what Nebula-specific types I can't replicate (like `UnityHelper`, `LayerExpansion`, `Virial.Color`, etc.) and map them to the project's equivalents.</think>现在我对 Nebula 的实现有了完整理解。核心区别：Nebula 使用 `SpriteRenderer` + `TextMeshPro` + `BoxCollider2D` + `PassiveButton`，而非 Canvas/Image/TextMeshProUGUI。需要完全重写以匹配 Nebula 的架构。

Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the job and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool
Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:
- Complex multi-step tasks - When a job requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Work that requires careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a job list to track the work
- User explicitly requests job list - When the user directly asks you to use the job list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as jobs
- When you start working on a job - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a job - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up jobs discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool
Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward job
- The job is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The job can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The job is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial job to do. In this case you are better off just doing the job directly.

## Job Fields
- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: Detailed description of what needs to be done, including context and acceptance criteria
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when job is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). This is displayed to the user while you work on the job.

**IMPORTANT**: Always provide activeForm when creating jobs. The subject should be imperative ("Run tests") while activeForm should be present continuous ("Running tests"). All jobs are created with status `pending`.

## Tips
- Create jobs with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- Include enough detail in the description for another agent to understand and complete the job
- After creating jobs, use job_update to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check job_list first to avoid creating duplicate jobs
- Use `allowDuplicate: true` only when you intentionally need a second open job with the same normalized subject

toolCalls.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

Writes content to a specified file in the local filesystem.

      Use this tool to create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file.
      Prefer the `replace` tool for targeted edits to existing files.
      Use `write_file` for new files or full-file rewrites.
      Do not use `replace` with an empty `old_string` to overwrite an existing file.
      Existing UTF-8, UTF-8 BOM, GB2312, and GBK text files are written back using their original encoding.
      New files use UTF-8 without a BOM. If updated content cannot be represented in an existing file's encoding, the write is rejected without modifying the file.

      The user has the ability to modify `content`. If modified, this will be stated in the response.

messages.content:
<think>There are several categories of errors:

1. **Default interface methods not accessible on LIDGUI class** — `RawText`, `RawButton`, `VerticalMargin`, `HorizontalMargin` are default methods on `IGUI` interface but C# doesn't allow calling them through the class type. I need to add explicit implementations on LIDGUI.

2. **UnityAction lambda conversion** — In Il2Cpp context, `AddListener` expects `UnityAction` not just `Action`. I need to cast lambdas with `(UnityAction)`.

3. **FindSoundClip not found** — It's a method on `VanillaAsset` static class but I removed the context. Need to call `VanillaAsset.FindSoundClip`.

4. **FindObjectsOfTypeAll with System.Type** — In Il2Cpp, need to use `Il2CppType.Of<T>()` instead of `typeof(T)`.

5. **Object ambiguity** — Need `using Object = UnityEngine.Object;` in Widgets.cs

Let me fix all these issues systematically.</think>有几个类别需要修复。我来系统地处理它们。

toolCalls.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

# HudUI 实现计划 — 基于原版 AU 克隆

## 目标
创建一套新的 UI 系统 `HudUI`，位于 `UI/HudUI/` 目录下。
与现有 `UI/Window/`（Nebula 风格 SpriteRenderer）并存，不替换。
通过克隆原版 Among Us 的 `DialogueBox`、`KillButton`、`PassiveButton` 等组件实现。

## 核心思路
- 克隆 `HudManager.Instance.Dialogue` (DialogueBox) 作为窗口基础
- 克隆 `HudManager.Instance.KillButton` (ActionButton) 作为按钮基础
- 使用 `DialogueBox` 的 `TextMeshPro target` 作为文本基础
- 使用 `HudManager.Instance.FullScreen` (SpriteRenderer) 作为遮罩

## 文件结构 (全部在 UI/HudUI/)

### 1. HudUI.cs — 核心
- `HudUIWindow` — 克隆 DialogueBox 的窗口
  - `Show(string title)` — 显示带标题的窗口
  - `Close()` — 关闭并销毁
  - `AddText(string text)` — 添加文本行
  - `AddButton(string text, Action onClick)` — 添加按钮
  - `Clear()` — 清空内容
  - `SetSize(Vector2 size)` — 设置窗口大小
- `HudUIButton` — 克隆 KillButton 的按钮
  - `SetLabel(string label)`
  - `SetSprite(Sprite sprite)`
  - `SetOnClick(Action onClick)`
  - `SetVisible(bool visible)`
  - `SetEnabled(bool enabled)`
  - `SetCooldown(float current, float max)`

### 2. HudUIHelpers.cs — 高级辅助方法
- `HudUI.OpenButtonWindow(string title, params ButtonOption[])` — 按钮选择窗口
- `HudUI.OpenConfirmDialog(string message, Action onConfirm, Action? onCancel)` — 确认对话框
- `HudUI.OpenMessageDialog(string message, Action? onClose)` — 消息对话框
- `HudUI.OpenTextWindow(string title, string text)` — 文本展示窗口
- `HudUI.OpenCustomWindow(string title, ...)` — 自定义内容窗口

## 实现细节
- DialogueBox 克隆：`Object.Instantiate(HudManager.Instance.Dialogue, parent)`
  - 访问 `dialogue.target` (TextMeshPro) 设置文本
  - 访问 `dialogue.BackButton` 控制返回按钮
  - 调用 `dialogue.Show(title)` 显示
  - 调用 `dialogue.Hide()` 隐藏
- KillButton 克隆：`Object.Instantiate(HudManager.Instance.KillButton, parent)`
  - 访问 `button.graphic` (SpriteRenderer) 设置图标
  - 访问 `button.buttonLabelText` (TextMeshPro) 设置标签
  - 调用 `button.SetCoolDown(current, max)` 设置冷却
  - 调用 `button.ToggleVisible(bool)` 控制可见性
- FullScreen 克隆：`Object.Instantiate(HudManager.Instance.FullScreen.gameObject, parent)`

## 验证
- `dotnet build` 编译通过
- 0 错误

toolCalls.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

toolCalls.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

| 文件 | 用途 | 精灵图布局 |
|---|---|---|

| `Checkmark.png` | 勾选标记 | 2列×1行 |
| `CloseButton.png` | 关闭按钮 | 2列×1行（普通/悬停） |
| `NavButton.png` | 导航箭头 | 2列×2行（左/右 × 普通/悬停） |
| `Background_Frame.png` | 窗口外框 | 九宫格，12px边框 |
| `Background_Inner.png` | 窗口内框 | 九宫格，8px边框 |
| `ColorButton.png` | 颜色按钮普通态 | 九宫格，4px边框 |
| `ColorButtonSelected.png` | 颜色按钮选中态 | 九宫格，4px边框 |
| `ColorFullBase.png` | 白色底 | 单图 |

### 按钮尺寸预设

| 预设 | 尺寸 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| `ButtonSize.Square` | 0.8 × 0.8 | 正方形按钮 |
| `ButtonSize.Rectangle` | 2.5 × 0.5 | 长方形按钮（默认） |
| `ButtonSize.SmallSquare` | 0.4 × 0.4 | 小正方形（如关闭按钮） |
| `ButtonSize.LongRectangle` | 3.5 × 0.5 | 长按钮 |
| `ButtonSize.Wide` | 4.0 × 0.6 | 宽按钮 |

### 使用示例

```csharp
using LightInDark.UI.HudUI;

// 现代风格按钮（三态精灵图切换）
var btn = HudUIButton.Create(parent, "技能", ButtonSize.Square, () => { });
btn.SetSelected(true);  // 切换到选中态
btn.SetSize(ButtonSize.Rectangle);  // 动态调整尺寸

// 颜色按钮（普通/选中两态）
var colorBtn = HudUIButton.CreateColorButton(parent, "选项", ButtonSize.Rectangle, () => { }, Color.Green);

// 窗口中添加按钮
var window = HudUIWindow.Create("标题", new Vector2(5f, 3f));
window.AddText("选择操作", 2.2f);
window.AddButton("确定", () => { }, ButtonSize.Rectangle, Color.Green);
window.AddColorButton("取消", () => { }, ButtonSize.Rectangle, Color.Red);
window.Close();

// 高级辅助
HudUI.OpenButtonWindow("选择", 
    new HudUI.ButtonOption("选项A", () => { }),
    new HudUI.ButtonOption("选项B", () => { }, Color.Green, ButtonSize.Wide)
);
```

sections.text:
## Available Sub-Agents
Use `task` for complex tasks requiring specialized analysis.

- **explore**: Fast read-only codebase search agent for finding files, patterns, and answering questions about the codebase. Use when you need to quickly find files by patterns, search code for keywords, or understand how parts of the codebase work. Specify thoroughness: 'quick' for basic searches, 'medium' for moderate exploration, 'very thorough' for comprehensive analysis.
- **general-purpose**: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.
- **plan**: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.


## Task Tool (Subagent Dispatch)

The `task` tool is the primary way to launch subagents for complex, multi-step tasks.
- For a single straightforward delegation, call `task` directly without creating a job.
- When a task corresponds to an existing planned job, pass `job_id` so the Task and Job systems stay linked.
- For simple, directed codebase searches (e.g. for a specific file/class/function), use `glob` or `search_file_content` directly.
- For broader codebase exploration and deep research, use the `task` tool with subagent_name="explore". It is faster and read-only. Use this when a simple search proves insufficient or when your task requires more than 3 queries.
- When the user asks to design, architect, or plan before implementing, use the `task` tool with subagent_name="plan" — it explores the codebase and returns a step-by-step plan with critical files.
